scene-1: [sighs] [somber, slow] It was late nineteen thirty-three... and the Great Depression was crushing New York City. [heavy, empathetic] Neville Goddard, far from his home in Barbados, found himself completely out of work... and, as he sadly put it, "didn't have a nickel to his name." [quietly] Thousands of miles from family... with no visible way back.
scene-2: [serious, deliberate] Seeking guidance, he went to his mentor and teacher — a mystic known as Abdullah. Neville poured out his desperate wish to be in Barbados for Christmas, confessing the cold, hard truth... zero funds. [pause] [intense, authoritative] Abdullah looked straight at him, and spoke five words that shattered Neville's reality... "You are ALREADY in Barbados."
scene-3: [curious, slightly confused] Puzzled, Neville tried to argue the facts — [firmly] but Abdullah cut him off. "You are in Barbados... and you WENT first class." [calm, reverent, slow] The instruction was radical. Don't try to go. Don't plan how to go. Instead... fall asleep tonight seeing America FROM Barbados. [softly] Live completely in the feeling of the wish fulfilled.
scene-4: [steady, measured] Night after night, Neville practiced this inner state. [tense, frustrated] Yet, a full week later... nothing in his outer life had changed. He returned to Abdullah, anxious to talk about his lack of progress. [stern, cold] Abdullah refused to entertain a single word about reality. He shut the door firmly in Neville's face... forcing him to live solely by his imagination.
scene-5: [quiet pause] Several weeks passed in silence. [excited, bright] Then... on the morning of December fourth, Neville spotted an envelope slipped under his door! It was from his brother in Barbados. Inside was a draft for fifty dollars... and word that a ticket was waiting for him at the shipping line! [energetic, rushing] He raced to the office, secured his passage — [slight pause, wry] only to be told that third class was all that remained.
scene-6: [warm, eager] When Neville rushed to tell Abdullah he had a third-class spot, [calm, amused, firm] Abdullah simply repeated his mantra... "Who says you're going to Barbados? You're ALREADY there — and you went first class." [triumphant, expansive] Two days later, on December sixth, Neville arrived to board the ship. At the last possible second, a first-class passenger canceled. Without paying an extra cent... Neville walked aboard into a luxury cabin.
